That has especially been the case in 2026, as MLS set a new single-season goals record on Wednesday night. Lucas Halter did the honors by scoring the 1,553rd goal of the season - surpassing the previous mark of 1,552 set in 2024 - during Houston Dynamo FC 's 1-0 win at Seattle Sounders FC . Several more goals followed on the night, and with two more Matchdays to go, this year's record may last for the foreseeable future. item.title: Vancouver Whitecaps take control of West on record-breaking night
item.description: Vancouver Whitecaps take control of West on record-breaking night By Alex Calabrese Vancouver Whitecaps FC are storming to the finish line of the 2026 MLS regular season. With a resounding 4-1 win over San Diego FC at BC Place and other results going their way on Wednesday night, the ‘Caps solidified their lead atop the Western Conference table (58 points). With that, Jesper Sørensen's side are closing in on securing the No. 1 seed in the West and, thus, home-field advantage all the way through the 2026 Audi MLS Cup Playoffs and possibly the Dec. 18 final. "I just have a good feeling about how we played. I know that everybody's focusing on the standings and stuff," Sørensen told reporters postmatch. "Last year we lost our last game and came in second instead of first, and it looked to be going up against. "So it's more, it's more important how we play and play." Historic display A year on from reaching the MLS Cup and Concacaf Champions Cup finals, the Whitecaps are looking to take a step further in 2026. With their four goals on Wednesday, they have smashed their club record for goals in a season , reaching 67 with two games to spare. Summer U22 Initiative signing Aleksa Cvetković got things started early, finishing off a penalty box sequence with for first MLS goal. Talisman Brian White headed home just before halftime to double the lead, and Ryan Gauld extended the scoreline to 3-0 early in the second half. Superstar Designated Player Thomas Müller was also introduced in the second half, marking his return from injury after almost a month out and adding an exciting boost to Vancouver's attack. Young Ecuadorian star Bruno Caicedo added the exclamation point with the record-breaking goal in the 76th minute, finishing off a fast break with his sixth tally of the season. The 21-year-old winger was named 15th on the league’s 22 Under 22 last week, and is quickly emerging as one of the MLS’ most exciting young prospects. White's milestone White’s first-half goal was his 18th of the campaign, but more importantly, it was his 100th career MLS goal. The former Red Bull New York SuperDraft pick has come into his own since moving to Vancouver in 2021, and now deservingly sits among the league's top strikers amid a career-best 18g/2a in 2026. "Something I've always wanted to get to and had my eyes on, if I'm being honest, to get to 100 goals," said White. "But at the end of the day, you want to win championships with the team to see like those things are nice, like you said, but you want to win MLS Cup. "I would win MLS Cup, and that's first and foremost on my mind." Vancouver need just one more win to secure the top seed in the West, with which they ensure home-field advantage in the playoffs at least up until the conference finals. It would also secure qualification to the 2027 Champions Cup. item.title: ‘He feels terrible’: Steve Kerr says why Yaxel Lendeborg is ‘not happy at all’ despite Warriors win
item.description: Photo by Godofredo A. Vásquez/Getty Images Golden State Warriors head coach Steve Kerr has claimed that Yaxel Lendeborg was not happy with his performance against the Minnesota Timberwolves. The Warriors have now won back-to-back games after starting the season with three consecutive losses. Their season looks to be back on track now, and Lendeborg has definitely played his part. Even against the Timberwolves, the 24-year-old produced a number of outstanding moments, but there were a few others that showed he needs to improve. Steve Kerr says Yaxel Lendeborg was feeling ‘terrible’ in the locker room Lendeborg recorded 26 points and eight rebounds in 35 minutes for the Warriors in their 119-114 win over the Timberwolves on Wednesday night. Usually, such a return is rewarded with a lot of praise, and he would be the hero in the locker room after the game. But that was not the case. That’s because Lendeborg committed seven turnovers in the game, which he knows is not good enough at this level. He just can’t be doing that. That is why he was devastated in the locker room after the game, despite all the other positives. Kerr said in his press conference : “We just show him the film and get him to understand time and score. The general idea is, if you have an advantage, take it. If you don’t, don’t try to force it. And he tried to force a bunch of plays tonight. “It’s his fifth game in the NBA. So, I’m really excited. I’m almost glad that’s happened. So, he feels it. He feels terrible in there. He’s not happy at all. “And yet, he had 26 points and eight boards in his fifth NBA game. So, it’s a great lesson for him. The simple play is the best one, over and over and over again. “And we have enough guys already on this team who are going to turn it over. So he needs to be solid. He needs to learn the value of just making the simple play.” Lendeborg not being happy with the turnovers he conceded in a game where he scored 26 points to help his side win speaks volumes about his mentality. It would be easy to ignore the negatives and just focus on the positives, but the fact that he was so upset shows he has the perfect mentality. However, as Kerr said, he’s only five games into his NBA career, so we’re sure moments like these will help him, not hurt him. item.title: Can Oilers’ Connor McDavid beat Wayne Gretzky’s unreal 50-point record?
item.description: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Can Oilers’ Connor McDavid beat Wayne Gretzky’s unreal 50-point record? appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid snatched another Wayne Gretzky record on Wednesday night. He provided two assists in the Oilers’ win over the Calgary Flames on home ice. This gives the Edmonton captain the longest season-opening assist record in NHL history. McDavid now has 36 points through 13 games after defeating the Flames. This is an incredible run that has not been seen in the NHL in decades. “Generational” is a word oft overused. In this instance, though, it absolutely fits. Edmonton’s captain is staring down the barrel of some incredible history this season. One of those major records is actually right over the horizon. Let’s take a look at whether Connor McDavid can take down Gretzky’s 50-point record in 2026-27. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Connor McDavid is chasing Wayne Gretzky’s 50-point record Perry Nelson-Imagn Images The record in question is the speed at which a player has reached 50 points in a single season. This record belongs to Wayne Gretzky. He scored 50 points in just 18 games during the 1983-84 campaign. Gretzky ended that season with 87 goals and 205 points. McDavid is currently on track to match this, at the very least. He has scored 2.77 points per game at this time. Across an 18-game stretch, this works out to about 49.86 points. If he maintains his current point pace, he can match this record. It’s also quite conceivable he surpasses it over the next five games. McDavid has to score 12 points in five games to beat the record. His season can be broken down into two five-game stretches. In his first five-game stretch, he scored three goals and 13 points. The second five-game stretch saw him score five goals and 18 points. McDavid has shown the ability to put up the points he needs in this short amount of time. Whether he can become the fastest to 50 points in a single season remains to be seen. However, at his current rate, it isn’t entirely out of the question this year. item.title: Knicks Notes: Jalen Brunson and the offense beginning to emerge; Tyler Kolek impressing
item.description: Knicks star Jalen Brunson didn’t shoot well in the first four games of the season. He also didn’t shoot well in the first four minutes of Wednesday’s game in Chicago. He missed three of his first four shots against the Bulls. At that moment, he was shooting 36 percent (31-for-86) on the season and 19 percent (4-for-21) from beyond the arc. If you were getting a little antsy in the opening minutes on Wednesday, Brunson probably put you at ease over the course of the night. The 2026 NBA Finals MVP hit six of his next nine three-pointers (12-for-21 overall) to help New York rebound from a 19-point third quarter deficit and take the second game of a back-to-back . He finished with a season-high 38 points, seven assists, and two steals in New York’s first road win of the year. The Knicks shot a season-high 46 percent from three and 45 percent overall in the comeback win. They looked like the potent offense that emerged late last regular season and then again in Game 4 of their first-round series win over the Hawks. For what it’s worth, Mike Brown was not panicked at all about his team’s shooting. "The biggest thing is: are we getting good shots from the right people? Watching the film and watching the game, I think we are," Brown said before the Knicks’ win over Detroit on Tuesday. "We’ve had some pretty good looks from the right people at the right time that normally go in so I want them to keep shooting." After a slow start, Brunson and his teammates certainly kept shooting - and shooting well - on Wednesday night. The difference for New York in the past two games has been taking care of the minor details on both ends of the floor. "(We’ve got to) focus on the little things until we get our rhythm. Once we get a rhythm, continue to do the little things. It' a big point of emphasis right no, our attention to detail." They executed enough of the little things and big things to leave Chicago with a win. Next up? Friday night in Philadelphia. Oct 28, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; New York Knicks guard Jalen Brunson (11) drives to the basket against Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis (14) during the second half at United Center. / Matt Marton-Imagn Images BROWN EXPERIMENTING If you see a lineup this season that you haven’t seen the last two years, don’t get alarmed. That’s Mike Brown’s way of stress-testing some ideas. "There’s some things that I’m looking at or messing with that may or may not stay the same," Brown said. "That’s part of what you’re trying to do to figure out what’s best for your team long term." One example? Brown played lineups with Jalen Brunson and Karl-Anthony Towns on the bench in the first two games. Brown abandoned that idea. But don’t be surprised if you see a few non-traditional lineups over the next couple of weeks as Brown gets a feel for this year’s version of the team. item.title: Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga face long road to redemption in China
item.description: People walk past a bus featuring French football star Kylian Mbappe (Jade GAO) Kylian Mbappe, Real Madrid and La Liga have apologised for the superstar striker's comments about Mao Zedong, but the damage to their reputation in China won't be easily or quickly repaired, experts say. The France captain, one of the best footballers on the planet, is at the centre of a major row after a video emerged this week of him appearing to make fun of former leader Mao. Mbappe talked about being amused by an internet meme of his face photoshopped onto "some guy, think he's a Chinese dictator". Mao remains officially revered as the hero of the communist revolution and founder of the People's Republic of China. He is blamed by historians for millions of deaths, but publicly mocking him is taboo, and Mbappe's remarks saw him become the latest foreign sports figure or entity to infuriate Beijing. Major Chinese brands cut ties with the 27-year-old, and Spanish top-flight matches will be pulled from state television broadcaster CCTV. Chinese state media and social media users lined up to lambast Mbappe, although they were left in the dark about what exactly he said. China has the world's second-biggest economy and can be hugely lucrative, and within two days the striker, his club Real Madrid, and La Liga all apologised. A spokesman for China's foreign ministry said the Beijing government took Mbappe's apology "seriously". - 'Serious damage' - So is that the end of the matter? "Viewed from a calm, objective and emotion-free standpoint, this is clearly a very damaging incident," Yan Qiang, a veteran sports commentator, told AFP. "It causes serious damage to the image of La Liga and Real Madrid in China. "In the age of the mobile internet things blow up on social media quickly and emotions run high. "An apology does not necessarily mean the end of the story. "It's better to have an apology than no apology at all, but it's definitely not the end of the story." The Mbappe furore and fallout is not an unfamiliar tale. Various overseas sports leagues or players have found themselves in hot water for comments on topics that are politically sensitive to China. China effectively cut ties with the NBA in 2019 after then-Houston Rockets general manager Daryl Morey tweeted his support for Hong Kong protesters. NBA executives said Morey had the right to freedom of expression. In contrast, La Liga immediately distanced itself from what Mbappe said. The NBA, which along with football is the most popular sport in China, was wiped from CCTV for more than a year. NBA pre-season matches only returned to China last year. Australian National University lecturer Debby Chan called the NBA case -- and now Mbappe -- an illustration of China's consumer nationalism, where online sentiment and state media converge into "a spiral of outrage". item.title: ‘We miss him’ — Tom Bischof looking forward to seeing Vincent Kompany back at Bayern Munich
item.description: (Photo by Jürgen Fromme - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich have continued to get the job done despite Vincent Kompany’s absence, with Aaron Danks stepping up t o lead the team during the head coach’s recovery. But while the results have remained positive, Tom Bischof admitted that something is inevitably different withou t the Belgian on the touchline. Asked whether things might be a little quieter in the dressing room without Kompany, Bischof praised Danks while acknowledging just how much the team misses their head coach. “I think Danksy is doing a good job too, and has a loud voice. He motivates us well, too, but of course, it’s a bit different wh en Vinnie is standing in front of us. We miss him, but we’re also happy that he’s doi ng much better now and is back home. We’re happy for him,” Bischof said (as captured b y @iMiaSanMia ). It is a nice insight into the atmosphere inside the Bayern dressing room. Danks has earned plenty of credit for keeping things moving, guiding Bayern to a 6-1 DFB-Pokal victory over FC Magdeburg, but Kompany’s presen ce clearly means a great deal to the players. The most encouraging news is that Kompany has been discharged from the h ospital and is continuing his recovery at home with his family. There is still no set timeline for his return, and Bayern are rightly allowing him all the time he needs. The players miss their coach, but his health comes first. Hopefully, it will not be too long before Kompany is back where he belongs — on the sidelines, leading Bayern Munich. Join the conversation! item.title: Borussia Dortmund’s Niko Kovač hoping for a speedy recovery for Vincent Kompany
item.description: Bayern Munich's Belgian head coach Vincent Kompany (L) greets Dortmund's Croatian head coach Niko Kovac ahead the German first division Bundesliga football match between Bayern Munich and Borussia Dortmund in Munich, southern Germany, on April 12, 2025. (Photo by Alexandra BEIER / AFP via Getty Images) / DFL REGULATIONS PROHIBIT ANY USE OF PHOTOGRAPHS AS IMAGE SEQUENCES AND/OR QUASI-VIDEO | AFP via Getty Images There’s been an outpouring of well wishes for Bayern Munich manager Vincent Kompany after he collapsed last Friday at Säbener Straße following Bayern’s first-team training session. The Belgian had just been getting over an infection as well as hip problems that had affected his ability to traverse the touchlines during Bayern’s last two matches, but it’s still unclear whether the collapse was related to the illness he was recovering from. Borussia Dortmund manager Niko Kovač, who previously managed and played for Bayern, offered his own well wishes for his rival manager ahead of Dortmund’s 1-0 win over Eintracht Frankfurt that provisionally took them to the top of the Bundesliga table. “Like all football fans, I wish him all the best. I hope he makes a speedy recovery and returns to the pitch as soon as possible. The most important thing at this stage is to give him some calm and quiet, because he needs time. We all know how demanding a coach’s job is, so I genuinely wish him all the very best. I hope we’ll be able to speak again at some point next week,” the Croatian manager gracefully said (via @iMiaSanMia ). Kovač is no stranger to the constant limelight and microscope Kompany is under as Bayern manager, and some reports have suggested that late nights, long days, and a relentless workload might have contributed to Kompany collapsing on Friday in addition to the illness he had been getting over. As the Croatian alluded to, Kompany will now be getting some proper rest as he recovers from what is always a concerning medical event, and he could wind up missing out on the season’s second installment of der Klassiker against Dortmund at the end of the month. That match will likely have big implications in the title race for the first time in quite a few seasons with the way things have gone so far. Join the conversation! item.description: Makinley Cooper-Johnson is one of three Welsh contestants on Beat Luke Littler [Supplied] A Welsh teenager will be aiming to bury Luke Littler on Friday evening – and use the six-figure prize money to become an undertaker. It is an unusual goal to have in mind as you prepare to step onto the oche to face the reigning world champion. But then it is not the norm to see a 14-year-old who only took up darts three years ago given a chance to topple the sport's leading light. Makinley Cooper-Johnson is one of the 24 contestants chosen by Netflix to take part in the streaming giant's Beat Luke Littler broadcast. A prize of £501,000 is on offer for the first to win a single leg of 501 against the world number one. 'Might Mak' is the second youngest to make it past the auditions after impressing the panel of judges, which included darts legend Phil Taylor. And after tips from the man they call the Power, the Wrexham rookie is not shy about his chances, either. "Look, I'm not saying I'm world-class or anything, but I can hold my own," Cooper-Johnson told BBC Sport Wales. "I've got a shot at this. "I respect Luke for what he's done. But at the end of the day, he knows he's good – but he doesn't know how good I am." Luke Littler won his first of two World Championships to date aged 17 [Getty Images] If he throws as well as he speaks, the affable youngster may well have a chance at scooping the life-changing sum. Promising to buy his brother a car is first on the agenda, and then setting up his own firm. "Undertakers never go out of business, do they?" he smiles. "Money's money! "Being successful is all I've ever wanted. Darts would be an amazing way to go for that, and I'd love to put some respect into the sport and hopefully achieve a lot. "But I also love to entertain, whether that's on a darts stage or a programme." A Freddie Mercury impression is part of his routine, and there were certainly no signs of being under pressure as hype around the programme builds, with Cooper-Johnson saying he almost didn't hang around to audition. "It was uproar when we got there," he said, mum Stacie adding that the family only found out his 'joke' application after receiving an invitation to try-out. "The queues were miles and miles of eager men and women all wanting to challenge one person, which is crazy to think about. "I'd had enough of standing around and was walking back to the car before a steward in a high-vis showed me the queues for under-18s. item.title: Luka Doncic-less Lakers get back on track with win over Clippers
item.description: JJ Redick has foreshadowed a night like Wednesday evening. When the Lakers would need to play or rely on players they normally don’t, for whatever the circumstances it may be for that given game. And against the Clippers, which was the second night of the back-to-back set after Tuesday’s home loss to the Trail Blazers , the circumstances were being without superstar guard Luka Doncic (back tightness) and Ziaire Williams (left foot soreness). Despite being without their best player and one of their starting wings, the Lakers got back on track after their first loss of the season, beating the Clippers 103-85. Collin Sexton defends Cam Christie during the first half of the Lakers’ 103-85 win over the Clippers on Oct. 28, 2026 in Inglewood, Calif. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill With Doncic sidelined, a significant amount of attention turned to Austin Reaves, the Laker’s second-best player who has gotten off to a career-best start to the season. The sixth-year guard has shown several times what he’s capable of doing when he’s the lone star in the lineup, recording box score numbers that rival All-NBA guards. Clippers coach Ty Lue acknowledged the threat Reaves poses. “He can beat you by himself. … He’s elite,” Lue said. And the Clippers treated Reaves as such, using aggressive defensive coverages to disrupt a rhythm that’s been challenging for opponents to slow down since the start of the season. Reaves finished with 16 points on 6-of-16 shooting to go with eight turnovers, ending his streak of 23-plus-point games while shooting at least 54% from the field in four games. But the Lakers didn’t need a nuclear performance from Reaves. They got Collin Sexton showing off why he’s nicknamed the “Young Bull”, with the veteran guard providing the “insanity”, as Redick put it, on both ends of the floor that the team has come to celebrate. Brook Lopez tries to make a pass around Jarred Vanderbilt during the first half of the Lakers’ win over the Clippers. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill They got Quentin Grimes, who stepped into the starting lineup for the first time, having his best two-way performance. And they got a near perfect shooting night from Matisse Thybulle . Sexton finished with 21 points, scoring nine straight points late in the third quarter that pushed the Lakers’ lead from 13 to 20 points. Sandro Mamukelashvili (left) celebrates with Walker Kessler after scoring during the first half of the Lakers’ win over the Clippers. AP Photo/Mark J. Terrill Grimes had a season-high 23 points to go along with five assists and four steals. Thybulle scored 15 points on 5-of-6 shooting (4 of 6 on 3-pointers). Veteran forward Jarred Vanderbilt made his season debut in light of the team’s injuries, finishing with an individual plus/minus of plus-22 in 21 minutes. item.title: No World Series miracle for weary Rays
item.description: Tampa Bay's Yandy Díaz reacts after flying out in the eighth inning of the Rays' loss to the Milwaukee Brewers in the World Series deciding game five (ELSA) After defying expectations with an American League-best 98 regular-season wins, sweeping the New York Yankees and besting Cleveland, the Tampa Bay Rays endured an all-too familiar World Series finish. The Milwaukee Brewers polished off a four-games-to-one victory over the Rays in Major League Baseball's championship showcase on Wednesday, leaving manager Kevin Cash "crushed" but grateful for the latest ride. "It's a special group," he said of the Rays. "They're banged up and hurting right now, but just grateful for the way they carried themselves all season long, winning a bunch of games. It's as close knit of a group as I've ever been around." After dropping the first three games to the Brewers the Rays rallied in extra innings in game four to stay alive. With the season still on the line on Wednesday pitching ace Drew Rasmussen took the ball on just three days' rest. "We knew it was a big ask," Cash said. "But appreciate Drew Rasmussen so much for taking the ball, wanting the ball and going out and doing what he did." Rasmussen allowed just one run over four innings, but the worn-out relief corps couldn't keep the Brewers in check. In addition, the Rays scored just 12 runs over the five games, going eight-for-39 at the plate with runners in scoring position. "Milwaukee Brewers pitching, it's as simple as that," Cash said of what caused the Rays' struggles at the plate. Some Rays players stayed in the dugout to watch as the Brewers celebrated the first World Series title in franchise history. "If it's something that you log in the back of your mind that, you know, you want to experience that, we want to experience that real soon here in the coming seasons," Cash said. "If it's better for that person or that individual that chose to sit and watch it, I can appreciate that." The Rays remain without a World Series title, having also come up short in 2008 and 2020. But even in the midst of the disappointment Cash said he was excited by the idea of what a returning core of Rays players could do next season. "Speaking of the guys who contributed to this postseason run, it's very easy to be excited, remain excited about the quality of players and people that we have coming," he said. bb/amz

(Photo by Caleb Bowlin/Getty Images) Getty The New York Knicks are searching. They have yet to replicate their NBA championship form so far in the new season. Mikal Bridges has been a bit part of the struggles, and that came to a head on Wednesday night in Chicago against the Bulls. Bridges appears to have gotten benched, at least temporarily. The Knicks subbed Bridges out with 8:09 left in the third quarter, and he didn’t play the rest of the frame or into the start of the fourth quarter. Barring a late change, that may have been Bridges’ last action of the night. Up to that 8:09 mark of the third quarter, Bridges had played 13 minutes. He had three points on 1-for-4 shooting from the field, including 1-for-2 from 3-point range. Bridges had yet to record a rebound, or an assist, or a steal, or a block. He had one turnover and was a minus-5. Why Did Knicks Bench Mikal Bridges? The Knicks can’t be happy with Bridges’ play so far this season. His non-impact 13 minutes on Wednesday night were just a continuation of what he’s done already this season — or more accurately, has not done. Bridges’ season game log before Thursday looked like this: 4 points, 3 rebounds 1 assist 0 points, 1 rebound, 4 assists, 1 steal 6 points, 5 rebounds, 1 assist, 1 block 12 points, 3 rebounds, 4 assists, 1 steal He has begun the year shooting just 9-for-33 from the floor (27.3%) and 4-for-18 from 3-point range (22.2%). That’s simply not good enough for a player who isn’t known as a great rebounder or passer. Bridges is an impactful defender when he’s dialed in, so that’s the one thing the Knicks really risk losing by not playing him. But given that the Knicks had begun the season just 1-3 and were then in a dogfight with the Bulls on Wednesday night, head coach Mike Brown must’ve felt it was time to shake something up. Bridges won’t be benched permanently, but a bit of an extended gap without him in the rotation was meant to force the Knicks to do something differently. Does Mikal Bridges Get Voided on DraftKings, FanDuel? The major sportsbooks have injury protection for NBA players, but Bridges doesn’t appear to qualify. For one, he did play four minutes in the second half, and a lot of the policies depend on something happening in the first half. And two, Bridges wasn’t injured, unless the Knicks say differently postgame. He seems simply to have been benched. It might just be a bad break for anyone who was counting on Bridges on Wednesday night. Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Tampa Bay Rays came up short in the World Series, but Kevin Cash was not shy about giving credit where it was due. After the Milwaukee Brewers closed out a 4-1 win in Game 5 on Wednesday night at Tropicana Field to capture the first championship in franchise history, the Rays manager singled out the unit that gave his team fits all series long. Cash said the Brewers have “as elite of a bullpen as I’ve ever seen,” via MLB Network . It is hard to argue with him. Milwaukee’s relievers were a constant thorn in Tampa Bay’s side , repeatedly slamming the door in close games and stranding runners in big spots. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Aaron Ashby was the headliner. The left-hander did not allow a run through his first 15 2/3 innings of the postseason, putting him second all-time for the most consecutive scoreless innings to begin a postseaso n, behind only Andrew Miller’s 16 in 2016. He also collected three saves, including the final out of Game 2 with the tying run on third base . Trevor Megill and Abner Uribe were just as reliable at the back end. Megill survived a tense ninth inning in Game 1, striking out Jonny DeLuca after a game-ending double play was overturned on replay. Uribe, meanwhile, picked up the win in Game 2 with 1 1/3 hitless innings. The bullpen came through once again in the clincher. Jacob Misiorowski tossed 5 2/3 scoreless innings before exiting with a cramp in his right calf, and Milwaukee’s relievers took it from there. Tampa Bay finally scratched across a run in the ninth, but Megill closed it out when Richie Palacios grounded out to end the series. Cash’s comments carry extra weight coming from a manager who has built his reputation on bullpen management . The Rays have long been known for their deep, creative relief corps, and Bryan Baker anchored their own bullpen with 41 saves this season. Still, there was no answering Milwaukee. The Brewers won three games in the series by three runs or fewer, with their bullpen protecting late leads each time. The Rays will head into the offseason looking to bounce back, while the Brewers can celebrate a championship that their relief corps helped deliver. But after a University of Utah video mocked his on-air persona, the ESPN personality found himself on the receiving end of the criticism he routinely dishes out. Former ESPN host Dan Le Batard is struggling to understand why McAfee appears to be taking it so personally, especially while McAfee is operating from one of the biggest platforms of his career. Dan Le Batard Questions Pat McAfee’s Expectations Discussing McAfee’s comments about Utah, Le Batard wondered whether the “College GameDay” personality had expected his larger-than-life personality to win over virtually everyone. “I really do think that Pat McAfee thought he was going to do some of these things and just be universally liked,” Le Batard said . He approached the controversy through McAfee’s familiarity with professional wrestling, where provoking a reaction is part of the spectacle. In Le Batard’s view, McAfee has built a successful career by embracing that polarizing persona, but now appears uncomfortable when the reaction turned negative. “I don’t know if Pat McAfee is enjoying as much of this experience as I feel like most of us think that he should be given that he’s on top of the world,” Le Batard said. item.title: Giants hand Devils first home defeat of EIHL season
item.description: Cardiff Devils won 5-2 at home against Belfast Giants in the league earlier in October [James Assinder] Cardiff Devils suffered their first home defeat of the Elite Ice Hockey League (EIHL) season as Belfast Giants claimed a 4-1 win at Vindico Arena. The Devils had boasted a 100% home record across 14 league, cup, and pre-season matches in 2026-27. After a goalless first period Belfast scored twice in the second through David Goodwin on the powerplay and Scott Conway. Logan Cockerill extended the visitors' lead early in the third, before Thomas Caron claimed his first Devils goal. However, the Giants restored their three-goal advantage with a Kaleb Pearson penalty shot. "With and without the puck, everything was tedious and looked like really hard work," said Devil's head coach Paul Thompson. "Take nothing away from Belfast they totally deserved the win and we just couldn't get it going." Cardiff remain top of the EIHL standings, with nine points from six games before hosting Guildford Flames on Saturday, 31 October. The Welsh club have also been confirmed as Challenge Cup semi-finalists following Sheffield Steelers 5-2 win against Manchester Storm. However, Devils back-to-back Cup wins last weekend - 4-2 at Nottingham Panthers and 1-0 at home to Steelers - could explain his side's lack-lustre showing against Belfast according to Thompson. "I don't make excuses and I think our fans know that," added the veteran coach. "I mean we're deeply disappointed but I know I pushed a lot of players and played a lot of players a lot of minutes last weekend and today we just looked like we didn't have any jump. "We were second to every puck and I know my own team, and I know how they can perform, and we weren't even at 50% of where I think that was and maybe the weekend took more out of us than I thought it would."

item.title: Cowboys Delay Injury Decision on $33 Million Star
item.description: Dallas Cowboys safety Jalen Thompson Getty It had been 14 years since the Dallas Cowboys, a team notably wary of paying out money in NFL free agency, had given out the kind of contract that was given to safety Jalen Thompson this winter, a three-year, $33 million deal to bolster the back end of the defense. Thompson played three games before he injured his hamstring, badly enough that he has been on injured reserve since. But his four weeks are up, which means the Cowboys are eligible to open the practice window on Thompson. They would then have 21 days to activate Thompson, or would have to move him to the season-long injured reserve. But to open the week of practice, the Cowboys have not indicated that they’re going to make that move on Thompson. Cowboys Still Unsure About Jalen Thompson Return For a Cowboys team that thought it had loaded up on safeties coming into the year, getting Thompson back would be big, because the depth has not panned out quite the way the team had hoped–PJ Locke has been injured, out with a torn plantar fascia (he is set to return), and rookie Caleb Downs has been more of a slot corner than a safety, at least when everyone is healthy. In setting the stage for the Cowboys practice week, coach Brian Schottenheimer laid out who was available. From Tommy Yarrish of the team website: “ Cowboys LB Dee Winters (calf) and S Jalen Thompson (hamstring) worked with director of rehab Britt Brown on the resistance cords today. Thompson, who has been on IR since September 30, has missed 4 games and can have his 21-day practice window opened. Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said yesterday the team had ‘not yet’ made a decision on opening his window.” Thompson, then, is highly unlikely to be back this week. But the Cowboys can start ticking off days until he gets there. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post Cowboys Delay Injury Decision on $33 Million Star appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: Republic FC’s Kyle Edwards making history as Sacramento prepares for playoffs
item.description: SACRAMENTO, Calif. (KTXL) — Sacramento Republic FC forward Kyle Edwards has developed a reputation for delivering when his team needs him most. Whether it's a late-game goal, a burst of energy off the bench or a game-winning finish, Edwards has become one of Republic FC's most valuable weapons heading into the USL Championship playoffs. "He's like a secret weapon. Although he's not so secret, but he's still very hard to stop," Republic FC head coach Neill Collins said. The numbers back it up. Edwards finished the regular season with seven goals in the final 15 minutes of matches, the most in the USL Championship. Four of those goals were game-winners. He also set a new league record with nine regular-season goals as a substitute, breaking his own mark of eight established in 2025. On September 26, Edwards also became the USL Championship's all-time leader in career regular-season goals scored off the bench. For Edwards, the records are rewarding, but the moments behind them mean even more. "It feels good. But I also know, like it's part of my job," Edwards said. "I'm happy that these goals come at very crucial times, and we can all celebrate it as a team and as fans and as a club as a whole." His ability to deliver in critical moments has made him a difference-maker for Sacramento. Edwards also became just the fifth player in Republic FC history to score at least 10 goals in his first season with the club. But his impact extends beyond the scoresheet. "We always know, like, if we're not playing good or behind, we know we have him on the bench who can bring a massive spark," teammate Blake Willey said. "And he always finds a way to deliver." It's a role Edwards has embraced throughout his first season with Republic FC, understanding that his contributions aren't always measured by goals. "Even if I don't score, I just got to bring the energy because that's something I can control," Edwards said. And when he does find the back of the net, there's a personal tradition that has become part of his celebrations. Edwards often pulls out a headband he keeps around his waist and puts it on after scoring. The message reads "100% Jesus," a tribute to the faith he says has guided his journey. "He blessed me with the talent, so I got to give back to him in any way possible," Edwards said. "And what more better way to give back to him than, you know, celebrating with him, scoring a goal." Edwards credits his upbringing and his mother, who raised him alongside his two brothers and sister, for shaping the person he has become. He also credits his teammates for helping him grow both on and off the field. Now, his focus shifts to the postseason, where Republic FC hopes to build on its regular-season success. item.title: Bulls Coach Tiago Splitter: 'We Got Better Tonight' in Loss to Knicks
item.description: Chicago Bulls forward Caleb Wilson speaks to the media following his team's 133-127 loss to the New York Knicks on Wednesday, Oct. 28, 2026. (Gavin Dorsey/Roundtable Sports) The Bulls don't count moral victories, but head coach Tiago Splitter recognizes that his young team is improving. Going against the defending champion New York Knicks on Wednesday night, Chicago played its best game yet this season. Although the Bulls lost, 133-127, Splitter's group had its most assists, fewest turnovers and best shooting percentage in the first five games. The team played collectively, rather than as a group of individuals, and it nearly resulted in the upset. However, the Bulls were outscored in the fourth quarter, 43-31. "We were focused for a longer period of time throughout the game, which is good, but the game still has 48 minutes," Splitter said. "That last quarter tonight wasn't good enough. Of course, they have great players... That's why they won the championship. But I think we competed for the most part. We got better tonight." After shooting a league-worst 23.8% on three-pointers through the first four games, the Bulls connected on 18 of their 42 shot attempts (42.9%) from beyond the arc. Norman Powell made four triples, while Matas Buzelis and No. 4 overall pick Caleb Wilson — who both struggled with accuracy to start the year — each made an efficient three shots from deep. Buzelis, 22, and Wilson, 20, are Chicago's two highest draft picks over the past three years. Both are close in size and play similar roles, but haven't quite found a fit alongside each other. Wednesday's game was a strong outing for the young duo, who combined for 37 points, 11 rebounds, seven assists, three steals and two blocks. Oct 28, 2026; Chicago, Illinois, USA; New York Knicks center Karl-Anthony Towns (32) fights for the ball against Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis (14), and forward Jalen Smith (25) during the first half at United Center. Mandatory Credit: Matt Marton-Imagn Images "I think they play better together," Splitter said. "And also, when they were not together, they were aggressive, trying to make plays, take care of the ball. We still got too many turnovers there sometimes, gotta be smarter in some situations. But again, I can go to sleep if we fight like this and compete every night." Midway through the second quarter, Wilson blocked Knicks guard Jordan Clarkson at the rim, then took the ball the other way in transition. From just inside the three-point line, the rookie forward lobbed a pass to Buzelis, who threw down the alley-oop jam. It was the first such connection between the two players this season. Buzelis and Wilson are widely expected to be the future of Chicago Bulls basketball. Although both can be prone to mistakes this early in their careers, the excitement they can generate was on display on Wednesday night. He allowed just two hits and reached 100 mph on 51 of his 86 pitches, including two pitches that hit 103 mph in the first inning. The title came one night after the Rays avoided a sweep with a 12-inning walk-off win in Game 4. Misiorowski made sure there would be no further drama. It caps a remarkable season for the 24-year-old , who went 16-5 with a 1.80 ERA and 252 strikeouts in the regular season. He led the majors in ERA, strikeouts and opponents’ batting average, and he is widely expected to win the NL Cy Young Award next month . The championship is the first for Milwaukee since the Braves won it all in 1957. The Brewers finished the regular season with a franchise-record 103 wins and went 11-2 in the postseason, knocking off the San Diego Padres, Los Angeles Dodgers and Rays. For Misiorowski and the Brewers, the wait is finally over. item.title: Coachella falls 5-1 against Tucson
item.description: Coachella Valley Firebirds forward Mitchell Stephens (67) wins a faceoff against Ontario Reign forward Kaleb Lawrence (22) during an AHL hockey game, Saturday, December 28, 2024 in Thousand Palms, Calif. PALM DESERT, Calif. — Behind Ben McCartney’s two goals, the Tucson Roadrunners picked up a decisive 5-1 win over the Coachella Valley Firebirds. Tucson improved to 5-2 on the season, while Coachella Valley fell to 3-4. Tucson’s five wins are the second most in the Pacific Division. "I’m not getting into it. I’m keeping that to myself," Coachella Valley head coach Derek Laxdal said when asked what isn’t working with the group. "There wasn’t much. There hasn’t been much good lately. You can talk about guys being in and out of the lineup, but that’s an opportunity for others to step up. We got some kids that are making the same mistakes night in and night out." Coachella Valley has lost back-to-back games and fell to a game under .500 on the year. The first period saw no scoring until the final 30 seconds, when McCartney scored his third goal of the season. Cameron Hebig was credited with the assist, his first of the season. The Roadrunners took full control of the game in the second period, scoring three of their five goals. Just two minutes in,Tij Iginla scored his first goal of the season. Joshua Roy and Montana Onyebuchi each were credited with an assist. The score became 3-0 when Austin Poganski scored his second goal of the season. Poganski’s shot hit the top of the net and crossed the goal line at the halfway point of the period. Zac Jones notched his fourth assist of the season, and Caleb Desnoyers added his third. Jones capped off a three-goal period for the Roadrunners at the 14-minute mark, assisted by Robbie Russo and Brandon Tanev. Jones’ goal silenced the crowd at Acrisure Arena. Penalties were a deciding factor against Coachella Valley in the second period, with 19 combined penalty minutes. Nathan Villeneuve was hit with a 10-minute game misconduct penalty after fighting prior to a puck drop. The second period ended with Tucson holding 24 shots on target, 10 more than Coachella Valley. It took just 23 seconds into the third period for the Firebirds to score their lone goal. Jagger Firkus scored his third goal of the season with assists from Kaden Hammell and Gustav Olofsson. Five minutes later, Tucson answered when McCartney scored his second goal of the game. Poganski and Hebig were credited with the assists. Coachella Valley continues its homestand Friday when it hosts the Henderson Silver Knights. Puck drop is scheduled for 7 p.m. at Acrisure Arena.
